title: ICSE CLASS 6 — Science | Garbage In Garbage Out
description: Subject-wise test on Garbage In Garbage Out (Science) for ICSE CLASS 6. 40Q.
subject: icse6-science

questions.question: Which of the following materials is generally considered biodegradable?

options.explanation: Plastic is non-biodegradable and takes hundreds of years to decompose.
Aluminium foil is non-biodegradable and does not decompose easily.
Vegetable peels are organic and decompose naturally.
Glass does not decompose and remains in the environment for a very long time.

questions.explanation: Biodegradable materials are those that can be broken down naturally by microorganisms over a period of time. Vegetable peels are organic matter and decompose easily.
questions.hint: Think about materials that can be broken down by natural processes.
questions.subject: icse6-science

questions.question: The process of converting organic waste like food scraps and garden waste into nutrient-rich manure is known as:

options.explanation: Incineration involves burning waste to reduce its volume.
Landfilling involves burying waste in the ground.
Composting is the process of converting organic waste into nutrient-rich manure.
Recycling involves converting waste materials into new products.

questions.explanation: Composting is a natural biological process where organic matter decomposes to form compost, which is a valuable soil conditioner.
questions.hint: This process involves breaking down organic waste to create manure.
questions.subject: icse6-science

questions.question: Among the '3 R's' of waste management, which one focuses on reducing the amount of waste generated in the first place?

options.explanation: Recycling involves converting waste materials into new products.
Reuse involves using items again for their original or a new purpose.
Reduce focuses on minimising waste generation at the source.
Repair is not one of the '3 R's' of waste management.

questions.explanation: 'Reduce' means to minimise the amount of waste created by consuming less, buying products with less packaging, and choosing reusable items.
questions.hint: This 'R' is about minimising waste generation at the source.
questions.subject: icse6-science

questions.question: Non-biodegradable waste materials are problematic because they:

options.text: Decompose very quickly and release harmful gases.
options.explanation: Non-biodegradable materials do not decompose quickly.

options.text: Can be easily broken down by bacteria and fungi.
options.explanation: Non-biodegradable materials cannot be broken down easily.

options.text: Do not decompose easily and remain in the environment for a very long time.
options.explanation: Non-biodegradable materials persist in the environment for a long time.

options.text: Are always safe to burn in open areas.
options.explanation: Burning non-biodegradable materials can release toxic fumes.

questions.explanation: Non-biodegradable wastes like plastics, glass, and metals persist in the environment for hundreds or thousands of years, causing pollution and harming ecosystems.
questions.hint: Think about how long these materials take to decompose.
questions.subject: icse6-science

questions.question: A family decides to use old jam jars to store spices and lentils, and old newspapers to make paper bags. This practice primarily exemplifies which principle of waste management?

options.explanation: Reduce focuses on minimising waste generation at the source.
Recycling involves converting waste materials into new products.
Reuse involves using items again for their original or a new purpose.
Refuse is not one of the '3 R's' of waste management.

questions.explanation: Reusing involves using items again, either for their original purpose or for a new purpose, extending their life and preventing them from becoming waste.
questions.hint: This principle involves using items again instead of discarding them.
questions.subject: icse6-science

questions.question: Why is burning plastic waste in open areas highly discouraged and harmful?

options.text: It helps in quickly reducing the volume of waste.
options.explanation: Burning plastic is harmful despite reducing volume.

options.text: It produces valuable ash that can be used as fertilizer.
options.explanation: The ash produced is toxic and not suitable for use as fertilizer.

options.text: It releases toxic fumes and harmful gases into the atmosphere.
options.explanation: Burning plastic releases toxic pollutants like dioxins.

options.text: It attracts beneficial insects to the area.
options.explanation: Burning plastic does not attract beneficial insects.

questions.explanation: Burning plastic releases dangerous pollutants like dioxins and furans, which are highly toxic and can cause severe respiratory problems and other health issues.
questions.hint: Consider the harmful gases released when plastic is burned.
questions.subject: icse6-science

questions.question: Assertion (A): It is essential to segregate wet waste from dry waste at home. Reason (R): Segregation allows wet waste to be composted and dry waste to be recycled more efficiently.

options.text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
options.explanation: Segregation of waste allows for efficient composting and recycling.

options.text: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
options.explanation: R correctly explains why segregation is essential.

options.text: A is true, but R is false.
options.explanation: Both A and R are true.

options.text: A is false, but R is true.
options.explanation: A is true.

questions.explanation: Segregating waste at the source prevents contamination. Wet waste is ideal for composting, and dry waste (like paper, plastic, metal) can be sent for recycling, making both processes more effective and reducing the amount of waste sent to landfills.
questions.hint: Consider the benefits of segregating waste at home.
questions.subject: icse6-science

questions.question: Which of the following is the most environmentally friendly way to dispose of a large quantity of rotten fruits and vegetables from a market?

options.explanation: Throwing waste into a river pollutes water bodies.

options.text: Burning them in an open field.
options.explanation: Burning organic waste releases harmful gases.
Landfills are not environmentally friendly for organic waste.

options.text: Creating a compost pit for them.
options.explanation: Composting converts organic waste into nutrient-rich soil.

questions.explanation: Rotten fruits and vegetables are organic and biodegradable. Composting them converts them into nutrient-rich soil, which is the most environmentally friendly and beneficial method of disposal.
questions.hint: Think about the best way to handle organic waste.
questions.subject: icse6-science

questions.question: A city implements a system where all collected plastic bottles are sent to a factory, melted down, and remoulded into new plastic products like buckets and chairs. This practice primarily helps in:

options.text: Increasing the demand for virgin plastic.
options.explanation: Recycling reduces the demand for virgin plastic.
Recycling conserves natural resources.

options.text: Conserving natural resources and reducing landfill waste.
options.explanation: Recycling helps conserve resources and reduces landfill waste.
Recycling does not promote open dumping.

questions.explanation: This process describes recycling. Recycling plastic reduces the need to extract new raw materials (like crude oil), saves energy, and significantly decreases the amount of plastic waste that would otherwise end up in landfills or polluting the environment.
questions.hint: Consider the benefits of recycling plastic bottles.
questions.subject: icse6-science

questions.question: You observe a large open dump of garbage near your neighbourhood. Over time, you notice a foul smell, an increase in flies and rodents, and liquid seeping into the ground. The liquid seeping from the garbage is called leachate, and its greatest long-term concern is:

options.text: It makes the soil more fertile.
options.explanation: Leachate is toxic and does not make soil fertile.

options.text: It helps in the growth of new plants.
options.explanation: Leachate is harmful to plants and does not aid their growth.

options.text: It can contaminate groundwater and nearby water bodies, making them unsafe.
options.explanation: Leachate can pollute groundwater and water bodies, making them unsafe.

options.text: It acts as a natural repellent for pests.
options.explanation: Leachate does not act as a repellent for pests.

questions.explanation: Leachate is a highly toxic liquid formed when water passes through decomposing waste. It carries harmful chemicals and pathogens, posing a severe risk of polluting soil and groundwater, which can have long-term detrimental effects on human health and ecosystems.
questions.hint: Consider the harmful effects of leachate on the environment.
questions.subject: icse6-science

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of biodegradable waste?

options.explanation: Plastic is non-biodegradable and does not decompose naturally.
Glass is non-biodegradable and does not decompose naturally.
Vegetable peels are organic and decompose naturally.
Aluminium is non-biodegradable and does not decompose naturally.

questions.explanation: Biodegradable waste can be broken down by natural processes (bacteria, fungi) into simpler substances. Vegetable peels are organic matter and decompose naturally.
questions.hint: Organic materials that can decompose naturally are biodegradable.
questions.subject: icse6-science

questions.question: The process of converting organic waste materials like kitchen waste and plant residues into nutrient-rich manure is called:

options.explanation: Composting converts organic waste into nutrient-rich manure.
Landfilling is a method of waste disposal, not a process of converting waste into manure.
Incineration involves burning waste, not converting it into manure.
Recycling involves reusing materials, not converting organic waste into manure.

questions.explanation: Composting is a natural process where microorganisms break down organic matter into humus, which is excellent manure for plants.
questions.hint: This process involves breaking down organic waste to create manure.
questions.subject: icse6-science

questions.question: Which of the "3 R's" primarily focuses on minimizing the amount of waste generated in the first place?

options.explanation: Reduce focuses on minimizing waste generation at the source.
Reuse involves using items again, but does not necessarily minimize waste generation.
Recycle involves converting waste into new materials, but does not minimize waste generation.
Repair is not one of the 3 R's.

questions.explanation: "Reduce" means to lessen the amount of waste we produce. This is the first and most effective step in waste management as it prevents waste generation from the start.
questions.hint: The first 'R' in the 3 R's focuses on reducing waste generation.
questions.subject: icse6-science

questions.question: If garbage is left open in residential areas, which of the following is MOST likely to occur?

options.text: It will quickly decompose without any issues.
options.explanation: Not all garbage decomposes quickly, and open garbage can cause issues.

options.text: It will attract beneficial insects and birds.
options.explanation: Open garbage attracts pests, not beneficial insects or birds.

options.text: It will become a breeding ground for disease-carrying pests like flies and rats.
options.explanation: Open garbage attracts disease-carrying pests.

options.text: It will improve the aesthetic beauty of the area.
options.explanation: Open garbage does not improve aesthetics and can cause pollution.

questions.explanation: Open garbage attracts pests like flies, mosquitoes, and rats, which can spread various diseases, posing a significant health hazard to the community.
questions.hint: Open garbage can lead to health hazards due to pests.
questions.subject: icse6-science

questions.question: Non-biodegradable waste materials are problematic because they:

options.text: Decompose very quickly, releasing harmful gases.
options.explanation: Non-biodegradable waste does not decompose quickly.

options.text: Do not decompose naturally and persist in the environment for hundreds of years.
options.explanation: Non-biodegradable waste persists in the environment.

options.text: Are always safe to be consumed by animals.
options.explanation: Non-biodegradable waste is not safe for animals.

options.text: Are easy to convert into useful manure.
options.explanation: Non-biodegradable waste cannot be converted into manure.

questions.explanation: Non-biodegradable materials like plastic and glass cannot be broken down by natural processes and accumulate in the environment, causing pollution.
questions.hint: Non-biodegradable waste does not decompose naturally and persists in the environment.
questions.subject: icse6-science

questions.question: Assertion (A): It is important to segregate dry waste and wet waste at home. Reason (R): Separating waste makes it easier for recycling and composting processes.

options.text: Both A and R are true, and R is not the correct explanation of A.
options.explanation: R correctly explains why segregation is important.

options.text: A is true, but R is false.
options.explanation: Both A and R are true.

options.text: A is false, but R is true.
options.explanation: A is true.

options.text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
options.explanation: R correctly explains the importance of A.

questions.explanation: Segregating waste is crucial because wet (biodegradable) waste can be composted, while dry (non-biodegradable) waste can often be recycled. Mixing them contaminates both streams, making effective processing difficult.
questions.hint: Segregation of waste helps in efficient recycling and composting.
questions.subject: icse6-science

questions.question: Which of the following methods of waste disposal is most suitable for disposing of hazardous hospital waste, such as used syringes and bandages?

options.explanation: Composting is not suitable for hazardous waste.
Landfilling is not ideal for hazardous waste as it can contaminate soil and water.
Incineration destroys pathogens and reduces waste volume.
Recycling is not suitable for hazardous medical waste.

questions.explanation: Hazardous waste, especially medical waste, needs to be disposed of in a way that destroys pathogens and reduces its volume. Incineration (burning at high temperatures) is often used for this purpose to prevent the spread of diseases.
questions.hint: Hazardous medical waste is best disposed of by burning at high temperatures.
questions.subject: icse6-science

questions.question: A city is experiencing severe problems with overflowing landfills and increasing air pollution due to burning garbage. Which long-term strategy would be most effective in addressing these issues comprehensively?

options.text: Build more landfills and encourage residents to burn their waste at home.
options.explanation: Building more landfills and burning waste are not sustainable solutions.

options.text: Focus only on recycling plastic and ignore other types of waste.
options.explanation: Ignoring other types of waste is not a comprehensive solution.

options.text: Implement a comprehensive waste management plan including source reduction, segregation, composting for organic waste, and recycling for dry waste.
options.explanation: This approach addresses waste management comprehensively.

options.text: Encourage everyone to throw all types of waste into rivers to get rid of it.
options.explanation: Throwing waste into rivers causes severe pollution.

questions.explanation: A comprehensive approach that includes reducing waste generation, segregating waste at the source, composting biodegradable waste, and recycling non-biodegradable materials is the most sustainable and effective long-term solution to manage waste and reduce pollution. Building more landfills is a temporary fix, and burning waste or throwing it into rivers causes severe pollution.
questions.hint: The best solution involves reducing, segregating, composting, and recycling waste.
questions.subject: icse6-science

questions.question: Imagine a school canteen generates a significant amount of food waste daily. To manage this waste sustainably within the school premises, which of the following would be the most appropriate and beneficial approach?

options.text: Collect all food waste in black plastic bags and send it to the nearest landfill.
options.explanation: Sending food waste to landfills is not sustainable.

options.text: Burn the food waste in a pit behind the school to reduce its volume.
options.explanation: Burning waste causes air pollution.

options.text: Set up a composting pit in the school garden to convert the food waste into manure for the garden plants.
options.explanation: Composting converts food waste into manure sustainably.

options.text: Ask students to carry all their food waste back home.
options.explanation: This is impractical and unsustainable.

questions.explanation: Setting up a composting pit is the most appropriate and beneficial approach. Food waste is organic and biodegradable, making it ideal for composting. This converts waste into valuable manure for the school garden, promoting sustainability and reducing the amount of waste sent to landfills.
questions.hint: Food waste is organic and can be converted into manure through composting.
questions.subject: icse6-science

questions.question: Why is it important to avoid throwing plastic materials into drains or water bodies?

options.text: Plastic quickly dissolves in water and adds nutrients.
options.explanation: Plastic does not dissolve in water.

options.text: Plastic helps in cleaning the water by absorbing pollutants.
options.explanation: Plastic does not help in cleaning water.

options.text: Plastic chokes drains, blocks water flow, and harms aquatic life.
options.explanation: Plastic causes blockages and harms aquatic life.

options.text: Plastic attracts fish, which then clean the water.
options.explanation: Plastic does not attract fish to clean water.

questions.explanation: Plastic is non-biodegradable and does not dissolve in water. When thrown into drains, it can block them, leading to waterlogging and breeding grounds for mosquitoes. In water bodies, it pollutes the water and is extremely harmful to aquatic animals who might ingest it or get entangled in it.
questions.hint: Plastic in water bodies harms aquatic life and blocks drains.
questions.subject: icse6-science

questions.question: Which of the following materials is generally considered biodegradable?

options.explanation: Plastic is a synthetic material that does not decompose naturally within a reasonable timeframe.
Glass is a non-biodegradable material that does not decompose naturally.
Vegetable peels are organic matter and decompose easily by microorganisms.
Aluminium foil is a non-biodegradable material that does not decompose naturally.

questions.explanation: Biodegradable materials are those that can be broken down naturally by microorganisms over time. Vegetable peels are organic matter and decompose easily, unlike plastic, glass, or aluminium, which are non-biodegradable.
questions.hint: Think about materials that can decompose naturally.
questions.subject: icse6-science

questions.question: The process of converting organic waste like food scraps and plant material into nutrient-rich soil enhancer is called:

options.explanation: Landfilling involves burying waste in the ground.
Incineration involves burning waste.
Composting breaks down organic waste into nutrient-rich soil.
Recycling involves processing materials into new products.

questions.explanation: Composting is a natural process where organic matter decomposes to form humus, which is a valuable soil conditioner. Landfilling buries waste, incineration burns it, and recycling processes materials into new products.
questions.hint: This process involves breaking down organic waste to create soil.
questions.subject: icse6-science

questions.question: Which of the "3 R's" focuses on finding new uses for old items instead of throwing them away?

options.explanation: Reduce means using fewer resources or products.
Reuse means using an item again for its original or a different purpose.
Recycle means processing materials into new products.
Repair is not one of the '3 R's'.

questions.explanation: Reuse means using an item again for its original purpose or for a different purpose, extending its lifespan. Reduce aims to lessen consumption, and recycle processes materials into new ones.
questions.hint: This 'R' involves using items multiple times.
questions.subject: icse6-science

questions.question: A student throws an empty plastic water bottle into the dustbin. Which type of waste has been generated?

options.explanation: Biodegradable waste decomposes naturally, which plastic does not.
Plastic is a non-biodegradable material.
Organic waste refers to biodegradable plant and food materials.
Green waste refers to biodegradable plant materials.

questions.explanation: Plastic is a synthetic material that does not decompose naturally within a reasonable timeframe, making it non-biodegradable. Organic and green waste refer to biodegradable plant and food materials.
questions.hint: Plastic does not decompose naturally.
questions.subject: icse6-science

questions.question: Assertion (A): It is better to use a cloth bag instead of a plastic bag for shopping. Reason (R): Plastic bags are non-biodegradable and harm the environment.

options.text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
options.explanation: The assertion and reason are both true, and the reason correctly explains the assertion.

options.text: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
options.explanation: The reason correctly explains the assertion.

options.explanation: Both the assertion and reason are true.

questions.subject: icse6-science

questions.question: Which of the following methods is *most suitable* for disposing of hazardous waste like old batteries or expired medicines on a large scale?

options.explanation: Composting is not suitable for hazardous waste like batteries or medicines.

options.text: Throwing them into a regular landfill.
options.explanation: Regular landfills are not equipped to handle hazardous waste safely.
Hazardous waste requires specialized treatment and disposal facilities for safe handling.

options.text: Burning them in an open field.
options.explanation: Open burning of hazardous waste is unsafe and harmful to the environment.

questions.explanation: Hazardous waste requires special handling due to its potential to harm human health and the environment. Composting and open burning are unsafe, and regular landfills are not equipped to contain hazardous substances effectively.
questions.hint: Hazardous waste needs specialized treatment.
questions.subject: icse6-science

questions.question: A family regularly separates their kitchen waste (vegetable peels, fruit scraps) from other household waste (plastic, paper, glass). What is the primary benefit of this practice?

options.text: It makes the kitchen smell better.
options.explanation: While it may reduce odors, this is not the primary benefit.

options.text: It reduces the total amount of garbage generated.
options.explanation: The primary benefit is not reducing the total amount but enabling proper disposal methods.

options.text: It facilitates composting and recycling processes.
options.explanation: Separating waste allows biodegradable materials to be composted and recyclables to be processed.

options.text: It saves money on garbage disposal fees.
options.explanation: While it may have indirect financial benefits, this is not the primary purpose.

questions.explanation: Separating kitchen waste (biodegradable) allows it to be composted, while separating other materials (like plastic, paper, glass) makes them easier to recycle. This sorting is crucial for effective waste management. While it might indirectly reduce overall landfill waste, the direct benefit is enabling specific disposal methods.
questions.hint: Think about the purpose of separating different types of waste.
questions.subject: icse6-science

questions.question: Ragpickers play an important role in waste management by:

options.explanation: Ragpickers do not create waste; they collect and sort recyclables.
Ragpickers collect and sort materials like plastic, paper, and metal for recycling.

options.text: Incinerating waste to reduce its volume.
options.explanation: Ragpickers do not incinerate waste; they collect and sort it.
Ragpickers do not transport waste to dumping grounds; they collect recyclables.

questions.explanation: Ragpickers manually collect valuable recyclable materials like plastic, paper, and metal from mixed waste, preventing them from going to landfills and providing raw materials for recycling industries.
questions.hint: Consider the role of ragpickers in the recycling process.

options.explanation: Vegetable peels are biodegradable and decompose naturally.
Fruit scraps are biodegradable and decompose naturally.
Used plastic bottles are non-biodegradable and do not decompose naturally.
Paper is biodegradable and can decompose naturally.

questions.explanation: Non-biodegradable waste includes materials that do not decompose naturally, such as plastic. Used plastic bottles are a common example of non-biodegradable waste.
questions.hint: Think about materials that do not decompose naturally.

questions.question: Which of the given items can be effectively recycled to make new products?

options.explanation: This excludes old newspapers, which are recyclable.
This excludes broken glass, which is recyclable.
Plastic bottles (1), broken glass (2), and old newspapers (4) are recyclable.
Leftover food (3) is not typically recycled into new products.

questions.explanation: Plastic bottles, broken glass, and old newspapers are commonly recyclable materials that can be processed into new products. Leftover food, being organic, is typically composted rather than recycled into new food items or similar products.
questions.hint: Consider which items are typically processed in recycling plants.

questions.question: What is the main component required for effective vermicomposting in compost pits?

options.explanation: Chemicals are generally avoided in organic composting.

options.text: Large amounts of water to keep it moist.
options.explanation: While moisture is important, it is not the defining component of vermicomposting.
Earthworms, especially redworms, are essential for vermicomposting.
Direct strong sunlight can be harmful to worms.

questions.explanation: Vermicomposting uses earthworms, especially redworms, to break down organic matter into nutrient-rich vermicompost. While moisture and warmth are important, the defining characteristic is the use of worms.

options.text: In a recycling centre or e-waste collection point
options.explanation: These centres are designed to handle hazardous waste safely.

options.explanation: Burning hazardous waste can release toxic fumes.

questions.question: Which process involves the burning of solid waste at high temperatures to reduce its volume?

options.explanation: Composting involves decomposition, not burning.
Landfilling involves burying waste, not burning.
Incineration involves burning waste at high temperatures.
Recycling involves reusing materials, not burning.

questions.explanation: Incineration is the controlled burning of waste at high temperatures, which reduces its volume and can generate energy.
questions.hint: Think about methods that involve burning waste.

questions.question: What is the first step Rahul should take to manage the waste effectively?

options.text: Burn all the garbage to reduce its volume
options.explanation: Burning waste can release harmful fumes.

options.text: Separate the waste into biodegradable and non-biodegradable categories
options.explanation: Separation is the first step in proper waste management.

options.text: Throw everything into a nearby dustbin
options.explanation: Mixing waste makes disposal less effective.

options.text: Dump it in a nearby water body

questions.question: Which of the following methods is used to separate plastic from other non-biodegradable waste for recycling?

options.explanation: Magnetic separation is used for metals, not plastic.
Plastic can be easily picked out by hand.
Sedimentation is used for separating solids from liquids.
Winnowing is used for separating lighter particles from heavier ones.

questions.explanation: Plastic is often separated by hand-picking because it is lightweight and can be easily identified and picked out from mixed waste.
questions.hint: Consider manual methods for separating lightweight materials.
questions.subject: icse6-science

questions.question: Which of the following is a consequence of improper disposal of plastic waste?

options.explanation: Plastic does not increase soil fertility.

options.text: Clogging of drains and water pollution
options.explanation: Improper plastic disposal clogs drains and pollutes water.
Plastic waste does not reduce air pollution.
Plastic does not decompose and slows down organic decomposition.

questions.explanation: Plastic waste, when not disposed of properly, often clogs drains, leading to waterlogging and pollution. It does not decompose easily and harms the environment.
questions.hint: Think about the environmental impact of plastic waste.
questions.subject: icse6-science

questions.question: Which of the following strategies would be most effective for reducing the amount of waste going to landfills?

options.explanation: Burning waste can release harmful fumes and is not sustainable.

options.text: Promoting the use of reusable bags and containers
options.explanation: Reusable items reduce waste generation at the source.
Increasing landfills does not reduce waste; it only manages it.

options.text: Encouraging people to throw more waste
options.explanation: Encouraging more waste generation is counterproductive.

questions.explanation: Promoting reusable bags and containers reduces the generation of waste at the source, which is the most effective way to decrease landfill use.
questions.hint: Consider strategies that prevent waste generation rather than managing it after creation.
questions.subject: icse6-science

questions.question: In a compost pit, which of the following combinations will lead to the fastest decomposition?

options.text: Dry leaves, plastic, and fruit peels
options.explanation: Plastic does not decompose and will slow down the process.

options.text: Dry leaves, vegetable scraps, and cow dung
options.explanation: All these materials decompose quickly and cow dung accelerates the process.

options.text: Metal scraps, glass pieces, and dry leaves
options.explanation: Metal and glass do not decompose and will slow down the process.

options.text: Plastic bottles, aluminium foils, and dry leaves
options.explanation: Plastic and aluminium do not decompose and will slow down the process.

questions.explanation: Dry leaves, vegetable scraps, and cow dung are all organic materials that decompose quickly. Plastic, metal, and glass do not decompose and will slow down the process. Cow dung acts as a natural activator for decomposition.
questions.hint: Consider materials that are organic and decompose easily.
